comment:
Read from the repository at commit 56bf82b, the tip of the default branch, whose plugin.json is byte-for-byte the installed one at version 2.0.0.

THIS MODULE IS NOT BUILT LIKE THE REST OF HETRICKCV. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), not getPolyVoltage, and the outputs are written to channel 0 alone, so the module is monophonic throughout. The phasor input also clamps to 0 to 10V (PhasorBeatMap.cpp:156) where the plugin's usual scaleAndWrapPhasor wraps; the sibling module PhasorWavetable in this same plugin does wrap. Neither difference is documented anywhere.

The phasor input is given no family, following the finished HetrickCV entry, where phasor jacks carry none either.

In Euclid mode the three left-hand knobs change job: Map X, Map Y and Chaos become the pattern lengths of channels 1, 2 and 3 (PhasorBeatMap.cpp:145-147), while the Fill knobs still set the fill. The Acc outputs then carry the point at which each channel's Euclidean pattern wraps rather than an accent (PhasorBeatMapPatternGenerator.cpp:285-295). None of this is in the README.

Chaos has no effect at all until the phasor returns to 0: the bar is redrawn only on a detected phasor reset (PhasorBeatMap.cpp:159-163).

The panel prints only the row and column labels: Phasor, Mode, Map X, Map Y and Chaos down the left, and the columns 1, 2 and 3 crossed with the rows Fill, Trig and Acc. The maker's tooltips name the channels Channel 1 to Channel 3; the original Grids calls them bass drum, snare and hi-hat, which is where the source's BD, SN and HH names come from.
